messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I had to run R CMD javareconf -e to first build. It gave me output [1]

(which links to  /usr/java/jdk1.6.0_16) jni.h exists there
but during the compile i see

gcc -std=gnu99 -I/home/sguha/lib64/R/include -I.
-I/usr/java/jdk1.6.0_16/jre/include
-I/usr/java/jdk1.6.0_16/jre/include/linux -I/usr/local/include
-fpic  -I/usr/include -c Rglue.c -o Rglue.o
In file included from Rglue.c:2:

Why isn't -I/usr/java/jdk1.6.0_16/include and why is ../jre/.. present?

Thank you
Sg

messages.subject: JGR crash on plot with upgrade to R 2.13.0
messages.subject_clean: JGR crash on plot with upgrade to R 2.13.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Several users on the Deducer list have experienced crashes when plotting ( http://groups.google.com/group/deducer/browse_thread/thread/49d2d65b2db919df ). I've determined that it is not deducer related, and am able to reproducibly crash my machine without Deducer loaded with the following code:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=mpg),data=mtcars)

Though interestingly, the following does not crash JGR:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x=mpg,y=cyl),data=mtcars)


The crash is reported as an invalid memory access:

Invalid memory access of location 0x10 rip=0x1218c331e

Segmentation fault

I tried with both the rJava available on cran, and the latest rforge version. Perhaps this is related to the infinite recursion bug I reported last month ( https://www.rforge.net/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=222 ).

Any thoughts?

Best,
Ian

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Several users on the Deducer list have experienced crashes when plotting ( http://groups.google.com/group/deducer/browse_thread/thread/49d2d65b2db919df ). I've determined that it is not deducer related, and am able to reproducibly crash my machine without Deducer loaded with the following code:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=mpg),data=mtcars)

Though interestingly, the following does not crash JGR:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x=mpg,y=cyl),data=mtcars)


The crash is reported as an invalid memory access:

Invalid memory access of location 0x10 rip=0x1218c331e

Segmentation fault

I tried with both the rJava available on cran, and the latest rforge version. Perhaps this is related to the infinite recursion bug I reported last month ( https://www.rforge.net/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=222 ).

Any thoughts?

Best,
Ian

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Is anyone on list able to reproduce this bug? Any thoughts on a solution? It seems like something low level in rJava, or perhaps JavaGD. I have tried and fail to track it down. Simon, I don't suppose you could provide any guidance?


Best,
Ian



On May 6, 2011, at 1:34 PM, Ian Fellows wrote:

> Hi,
> 
> Several users on the Deducer list have experienced crashes when plotting ( http://groups.google.com/group/deducer/browse_thread/thread/49d2d65b2db919df ). I've determined that it is not deducer related, and am able to reproducibly crash my machine without Deducer loaded with the following code:
> 
> data(mtcars)
> library(ggplot2)
> ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=mpg),data=mtcars)
> 
> Though interestingly, the following does not crash JGR:
> 
> data(mtcars)
> library(ggplot2)
> ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x=mpg,y=cyl),data=mtcars)
> 
> 
> The crash is reported as an invalid memory access:
> 
> Invalid memory access of location 0x10 rip=0x1218c331e
> 
> Segmentation fault
> 
> I tried with both the rJava available on cran, and the latest rforge version. Perhaps this is related to the infinite recursion bug I reported last month ( https://www.rforge.net/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=222 ).
> 
> Any thoughts?
> 
> Best,
> Ian

messages.subject: JGR + R 2.13.0 on Mac OS X: please update R
messages.subject_clean: JGR + R 2.13.0 on Mac OS X: please update R
messages.body_plain:
To all users using JGR with R 2.13.0 on Mac OS X:
please update your R to the latest R 2.13.0 patched from
http://r.research.att.com/

The direct link is
http://r.research.att.com/R-2.13-branch-leopard.pkg


Background: R 2.13.0 started using OpenMP to parallelized internal computations if they are large enough. Although the idea is good, there is a bug in gcc-4.2 (which is what Apple is using) such that it will crash when run in parallel with other threads. This means that R will crash in JGR which runs R in one of Java threads. Since R parallelizes only under certain conditions the effect is that you will see seemingly random crashes in JGR. To fix that, the current builds of R don't use OpenMP. It is not as bad as it sounds, because OpenMP (as implemented by gcc) has performance issues on Mac OS X which we are investigating.

The JDK is probably complete, but its installer didn't create a link for 
javah in the /usr/bin directory. R expect javah in /usr/bin, it doesn't 
check the java home directory. You can create the link manually as root:

ln -s /usr/java/default/bin/javah /usr/bin

Simon, is it possible to force R that it picks only JAVA_HOME and not 
the links in /usr/bin?

information would be useful for anybody who could help me.

SigmaXL, both of which require Windows OS.  A GUI is necessary for
practical use of R in my quality management activities.

results and experience is quite encouraging.

Couple of days back there was a large on-line update (SuSE linux 11.4)
in the system and JGR stopped working.  I tried uninstall/reinstall of
R, R-Devel, Java, from the SuSE repositories.  However, I am unable to

messages.subject: Passing Date objects between R and Java [Was: rJava]
messages.subject_clean: Passing Date objects between R and Java [Was: rJava]
messages.body_plain:
On May 27, 2011, at 11:16 AM, Lodha, Akhil wrote:

> Thanks Simon. Sure you can CC this to stats-rosuda-devel.
> 
> Couple of more questions/comments:
> 
> 1. If I have java code that returns data to R. Can I not do anything in Java so that I have to do minimal work for the date/time conversion in R ? Right now I'm returning date/time as string in format "yyyy-mm-dd HH:mm:ss z". I realized that I would have to change the format to "yyyy/mm/dd HH:mm:ss z".

R doesn't care - when using strings you can specify any format you want (see ?strptime). It's just that using string is very inefficient so I tend to avoid it (string date handling is unusable with large data).


> 2. In general people will have big vectors of date/time objects. It might be slow to iterate through each member in a loop and do the conversion using the method you described below. Is there a faster way ?
> 

Well, the fastest is to pass them as a vector - but that you would have to do in Java:

public class JJ {
public static long[] dates2R(Date[] dates) {
long res[] = new long[dates.length]; for (int i = 0; i < dates.length; i++) res[i] = dates[i].getTime(); 
return res;
}
}

the rest is the same:

> v = .jcall("JJ","[J","dates2R",javaDates) / 1000
> attributes(v)=attributes(as.POSIXct("2000-01-01"))
> v
[1] "2011-01-01 00:00:00 EST" "2011-01-02 08:00:00 EST"

Obviously, you could get them as strings but that is less efficient (see above)

Cheers,
Simon


> -----Original Message-----
> From: Simon Urbanek [mailto:simon.urbanek at r-project.org]
> Sent: Friday, May 27, 2011 10:50 AM
> To: Lodha, Akhil [ICG-MKTS]
> Subject: Re: rJava
> 
> On May 27, 2011, at 10:28 AM, Lodha, Akhil wrote:
> 
>> I was wondering if there is an easy way to convert Java Date/time objects to R Date/time format or what is the recommended way ?
>> 
> 
> Both Java and R use the same time representation (POSIX time) so they don't need any conversion (except that Java uses milliseconds, everyone else uses seconds). The only slightly annoying fact is that R (surprisingly) doesn't have an easy way to get from POSIX time to a POSIXct objects (even though it's essentially the same), so I use a very efficient hack that just adds the correct attributes from any random POSIXct object:
> 
>> d = .jnew("java/util/Date","2011/01/01 08:00")  ## create a Java Date object
>> v = .jcall(d,"J","getTime")/1000  ## get the POSIX time from the Java object
>> v
> [1] 1293886800
>> attributes(v)=attributes(as.POSIXct("2000-01-01"))  ## copy attributes from any POSIXct object (the date doesn't matter, only tz does)
>> v
> [1] "2011-01-01 08:00:00 EST"
> 
> If you want to change the timezone, just set the "tz" argument of the as.POSIXct above (the default is your current time zone)
> 
> (Do you mind if I CC this to stats-rosuda-devel for posterity which is the rJava mailing list where the questions should go?).
> 
> Cheers,
> Simon
> 
>

No, it is the actual configuration log which is in rJava/config.log after you tried to install it. It has the actual commands that configure is running an their results - i.e., the reasons why the output say yes/no/error.
Probably the easiest way to get at it (because R usually removes the build directory on failure) is something like
> download.packages("rJava",".",type='source')

and then in the shell:

tar fxz rJava_0.8-8.tar.gz
R CMD INSTALL rJava
then send rJava/config.log
(it's ok to just send it to me).

Thanks,
Simon

On May 30, 2011, at 11:34 AM, Vikas Garud wrote:

>> No, it is the actual configuration log which is in rJava/config.log after you tried to install SNIP

>> (it's ok to just send it to me).

>> Simon
> 
> 
> Thanks.  The log file is attached.
> 

configure:4178: ./conftest
./conftest: error while loading shared libraries: libjvm.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory


Apparently libjvm.so is not on your LD_LIBRARY_PATH. This means, that your Java setup is in some way non-standard, because R is usually able to detect it and set it accordingly. To fix that, search in your Java to find libjvm.so and add that path to LD_LIBRARY_PATH (you may also need to add dependencies if there are any). If that works you can edit etc/ldpaths in your R (the second line R_JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH) to adjust it.

Cheers,
Simon
